title: Dissociative amnesias in everyday life
summary:
Dissociative amnesias are a form of memory or time gaps that occur in everyday life and can significantly impair quality of life in people who suffer from so-called dissociative disorders.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether regularly taking photographs in everyday life and reviewing them can serve as a memory aid for individuals with dissociative amnesia, thereby reducing the perceived time gaps, lessening the perceived distress, and increasing sense of control over their own actions.

Patients with dissociative disorders who report experiencing dissociative amnesias in everyday life will be enrolled, after receiving comprehensive information and giving informed consent. Study participants will be randomly assigned to two groups.

In the intervention group (Arm 1), participants will regularly take photographs of their daily routines for two weeks. At the end of each day, they will be asked to review the photos and indicate the number of remaining time gaps. The examination phase will be preceded by a two-week period, during which participants report the number of time gaps they experienced, without being actively asked to take photographs.

The control group (Arm 2) will be asked about the occurrence of time gaps throughout the entire period, but without being asked to take and view photographs. This will allow for the analysis of differences both within and between the groups.

The study aims to provide insights into the occurrence of dissociative amnesias, as well as to demonstrate a possible positive impact of photography on the perception of these amnesias and on the quality of life and self-efficacy of those affected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with dissociative disorders (ICD-10: F44).
Report of time gaps in daily life at study start.
Exclusion criteria:
Previous brain surgery. Certain infectious and parasitic diseases (ICD-10 A00-B99), malignant tumor diseases (ICD-10 C00-C97), organic mental disorders (ICD-10 F00-F09), serious mental and behavioral disorders due to psychotropic substances (from ICD-10 F10-F19), schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders (ICD-10 F20-F29), intellectual disabilities (ICD-10 F70-F79), developmental disorders (ICD-10 F80-F89), systemic atrophies predominantly affecting the central nervous system (ICD-10 G10-G14), other degenerative diseases of the nervous system (ICD-10 G30-G32), cerebrovascular diseases (ICD-10 I60-I69), pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period (ICD-10 O00-O99).
